10.sol: Stele is a column containing vascular tissues which is surrounded by pericycle and separated from ground tissue by endodermis. 79902.subject: Botany
79902.text: In an ecosystem if the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of first trophic level is 100 x ( kcal m ⁻² ) yr ⁻¹ , what would be the GPP (Gross Primary Productivity) of the third trophic level of the same ecosystem?
79902.sol: NPP at first trophic level would be the GPP for second trophic level. NPP at second trophic level would be GPP for third trophic level. 79915.sol: There are certain limitation of ecological pyramids. Such as : - It does not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels. - It assumes a simple food chain, something that almost never exists in nature. - It does not accommodate a food web. - Saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids even though they play a vital role in the ecosystem.

Drug addicts are least susceptible to HIV infection
AIDS patients are being fully cured cent per cent with proper care and nutrition
The causative HIV retrovirus enters helper T-lymphocytes thus reducing their numbers
84525.sol: AIDS (Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome) is a viral disease of immune system. It is caused by virus Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). In AIDS patients, the virus homes on CD ₄+ T-cells (helper T-lymphocytes), infecting and killing them until none are left. Without their crucial immune system cells, the body cannot mount a defence against invading bacteria or viruses. AIDS patient die off infections that a healthy person could fought off.

The start codon always codes for methionine in eukaryotes and a modified methionine, i.e., fMet in prokaryotes. Termination codons or stop codon is a nucleotide triplet within messenger RNA that signals translational termination.

85053.text: Match List-I with List-II . List-I List-II A. Both species are harmed I. Predation B. One species is harmed and the other is benefited II. Mutualism C. Both species are benefited III. Competition D. One is benefited while the other has no effect IV. Commensalism Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
85053.sol: In competition, both interacting species are harmed as they compete for the same limited resources. Thus, A matches III. In predation, one species (predator) benefits while the other (prey) is harmed. Thus, B matches I. In mutualism, both interacting species benefit from each other. Thus, C matches II. In commensalism, one species benefits while the other is neither harmed nor benefited (no effect). Thus, D matches IV. The correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

121482.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. The criterias for five kingdom classification included appearances of an organism 2. The criterias for five kingdom classification included mode of nutrition 3. The criterias for five kingdom classification included phyllogenetic relationships 4. The three-domain system has also been proposed that divides the Kingdom protista into two domains.
121482.sol: R.H. Whittaker (1969) proposed a Five Kingdom Classification. The main criteria for classification used by him include cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships. The three-domain system has also been proposed that divides the Kingdom Monera into two domains, leaving the remaining eukaryotic kingdoms in the third domain and thereby a six kingdom classification.

121527.subject: Botany
121527.text: What are the four major groups of Protozoa?
121527.sol: The four major groups of Protozoa are Amoeboid protozoans, flagellated protozoans , Ciliated protozoans and sporozoans.

121536.subject: Botany
121536.text: Contagium vivum fluidum was proposed by
121536.sol: Contagium vivum fluidum was proposed by M.W. Beijerinck.

121665.subject: Botany
121665.text: There exists a close association between the alga and the fungus within a lichen. The fungus
options: fixes the atmospheric nitrogen for the alga
provides protection, anchorage and absorption for the alga
121665.sol: Lichen is a symbiotic association between a fungus and an algae (green alga or blue green alga). The algal partner of lichen is called as phycobiont while fungal partner is termed as mycobiont. Lichen develops into a unique morphological form which is quite distinct from either partner. The fungal partner of lichen helps in the absorption of water and mineral to algal partner additionally it also provides protection and anchorage to algal partner of lichen. In exchange of this, the fungal partner absorbs prepared f

122030.subject: Botany
122030.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Selaginella and Salvinia represent an event that is considered an important step in evolution as a precursor to the seed habit. Reason (R): These plants produce two kinds of spores, and their female gametophytes are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods. In the light of the above
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
122030.sol: According to NCERT, genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores are known as heterosporous. In these plants, the female gametophytes are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods. The development of the zygotes into young embryos takes place within the female gametophytes. This retention and in-situ development is a precursor to the seed habit, which is considered an important step in evolution. Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are correct, and the Reason correctly expla

122069.subject: Botany

one can conclude that the plant is apomictic
there is no change in success rate of fertilization.
122069.sol: In the prothallus of a vascular cryptogam, the antherozoids and eggs mature atdifferent times which result in failurity of self-fertilization.

122437.subject: Botany
122437.text: Germinal Layers Types A. Diploblastic 1. Two embryonic layers B. Triploblastic 2. Three embryonic layers C. Monoblastic 3. Four embryonic layers D. Tetraplastic 4. One embryonic layer
122437.sol: Diploblastic animals have two embryonic layers, triploblastic animals have three layers, and monoblastic and tetraplastic layers are not mentioned.

123174.subject: Botany
123174.text: Coffee and quinine are obtained from the
123174.sol: Coffea arabica (Rubiaceae) yields the well known beverage coffee. Cinchona sp. (Rubiaceae) yields the quinine which is used in treatment of malaria.

123240.subject: Botany
123240.text: Which type of cells in the mesophyll are oval or round and loosely arranged?
123240.sol: The vertical section of a dorsiventral leaf through the lamina shows three main parts, namely, epidermis, mesophyll and vascular system. The epidermis which covers both the upper surface (adaxial epidermis) and lower surface (abaxial epidermis) of the leaf has a conspicuous cuticle. The abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis. The latter may even lack stomata. The tissue between the upper and the lower epidermis is called the mesophyll. Mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and c

123598.subject: Botany
123598.text: At which stage of mitosis are chromosomes most easily studied?
123598.sol: The complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the start of the second phase of mitosis, hence the chromosomes are spread through the cytoplasm of the cell. By this stage, condensation of chromosomes is completed and they can be observed clearly under the microscope. This then, is the stage at which morphology of chromosomes is most easily studied. At this stage, metaphase chromosome is made up of two sister chromatids, which are held together by the centromere.

123614.subject: Botany
123614.text: What is the purpose of the metaphase stage in mitosis?
options: To align the chromosomes at the spindle equator
To move the chromosomes to opposite poles of the cell
To initiate the condensation of chromosomal material
123614.sol: Hence, the metaphase is characterised by all the chromosomes coming to lie at the equator with one chromatid of each chromosome connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from one pole and its sister chromatid connected by its kinetochore to spindle fibres from the opposite pole. The key features of metaphase are: Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores ofchromosomes. Chromosomes are moved to spindle equator and get aligned along metaphase plate through spindle fibres to both poles.

123617.subject: Botany
123617.text: What are the two daughter chromatids referred to as during anaphase?
options: Daughter chromosomes of the future daughter nuclei
123617.sol: At the onset of anaphase, each chromosome arranged at the metaphase plate is split simultaneously and the two daughter chromatids, now referred to as daughter chromosomes of the future daughter nuclei , begin their migration towards the two opposite poles. each chromosome moves away from the equatorial plate, the centromere of each chromosome remains directed towards the pole and hence at the leading edge, with the arms of the chromosome trailing behind. Thus, anaphase stage is characterised by the following key ev

123638.subject: Botany
123638.text: What is the name of the process that completes cell division by separating the cytoplasm into two daughter cells?
123638.sol: Mitosis accomplishes not only the segregation of duplicated chromosomes into daughter nuclei (karyokinesis), but the cell itself is divided into two daughter cells by the separation of cytoplasm called cytokinesis at the end of which cell division gets completed. In an animal cell, this is achieved by the appearance of a furrow in the plasma membrane. The furrow gradually deepens and ultimately joins in the centre dividing the cell cytoplasm into two. Plant cells however, are enclosed by a relatively inextensible c

123653.subject: Botany
123653.text: What happens to the chromosome number during meiosis?
123653.sol: The production of offspring by sexual reproduction includes the fusion of two gametes, each with a complete haploid set of chromosomes. Gametes are formed from specialised diploid cells. This specialised kind of cell division that reduces the chromosome number by half results in the production of haploid daughter cells. This kind of division is called meiosis. Meiosis ensures the production of haploid phase in the life cycle of sexually reproducing organisms whereas fertilisation restores the diploid phase. . We co

123846.subject: Botany
123846.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II (A) Zygotene (I) Terminalisation of chiasmata (B) Pachytene (II) Chiasmata formation (C) Diplotene (III) Crossing over (D) Diakinesis (IV) Synapsis Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
123846.sol: Zygotene is the second stage of prophase I, characterised by the pairing of homologous chromosomes, a process called synapsis. Pachytene is the third stage, during which crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes. Diplotene is the fourth stage, marked by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the formation of X-shaped structures called chiasmata. Diakinesis is the final stage of prophase I, marked by the terminalisation of chiasmata. Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-

123851.subject: Botany
123851.text: A diploid animal cell with 2n = 16 is undergoing meiosis. How many centromeres and chromatids, respectively, will be observed moving towards each pole during Anaphase I?
123851.sol: During Anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes separate and move towards opposite poles, but the centromeres do not split. Since the diploid number is 2n = 16 , there are 16 chromosomes in total. During Anaphase I, half of the chromosomes (8 chromosomes) move to each pole. Because the centromeres remain intact, each of these 8 chromosomes still consists of two sister chromatids. Therefore, there are 8 centromeres and 8 2 = 16 chromatids moving towards each pole. Answer: 8 centromeres and 16 chromatids

124020.subject: Botany
124020.text: What is the main function of the golgi apparatus?
options: Transporting materials to the cell membrane
124020.sol: The golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials , to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell. Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing face. This explains, why the golgi apparatus remains in close association with the endoplasmic reticulum. A number of proteins synthesized by ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum are modified in the cisternae of the gol

124350.subject: Botany
124350.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Chloroplasts are considered semi-autonomous organelles. Reason (R): Chloroplasts possess their own single circular double-stranded DNA molecule and 70S ribosomes, allowing them to synthesize some of their required proteins. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer fr
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
124350.sol: Chloroplasts (along with mitochondria) are unique among eukaryotic organelles because they possess their own genetic material and protein synthesis machinery. The stroma of chloroplasts contains small, single, circular, double-stranded DNA molecules and 70S ribosomes. This allows them to synthesize some of the proteins required for their functioning, making them semi-autonomous organelles. Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). Answer: Both (A) and (R) are

124359.subject: Botany
124359.text: A microscopic organism is found to have double-stranded, circular DNA that is not associated with basic proteins such as histones. Which of the following structural features is expected to be present in this organism?
options: Presence of 80S ribosomes in the cytoplasm
A well-defined nucleus enclosed by a nuclear envelope
Presence of 70S ribosomes in the cytoplasm
Presence of mitochondria for ATP synthesis
124359.sol: The presence of double-stranded, circular DNA without histone proteins (naked DNA) is a characteristic feature of prokaryotic cells. Prokaryotic cells lack a well-defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria. They exclusively possess 70S ribosomes in their cytoplasm, whereas eukaryotic cells have 80S ribosomes in their cytoplasm. Answer: Presence of 70S ribosomes in the cytoplasm

124401.subject: Botany
124401.text: Assertion : Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous organelles. Reason : They are formed by division of preexisting organelles as well as contain DNA but lack protein synthesizing machinery.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
124401.sol: Mitochondria and chloroplasts both are double membrane organelles. They are semi autonomous as both their structure and functions are partially controlled by nucleus of the cell and partially themselves. Both possess their own DNA and arises from pre-existing cells. Synthesis of many amino acids occurs in mitochondria. The first formed amino acids are glutamic acid and aspartic acid. Plastid also manufacture some of its own proteins, enzymes and other chemicals because of the presence of 70 ~s ribosomes which can h

124478.subject: Botany
124478.text: What is growth in living beings?
options: An irreversible permanent increase in size
124478.sol: Growth can be defined as an irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ or its parts or even of an individual cell. The swelling of a piece of wood when placed in water is an example of temporary swelling. It isn't growth or permanent increase in size as it can shrink back to the original size after removing it from water.

In only a fewsystems, the initial growth is

125260.sol: Plants require nutrients for proper growth and development. 16 elements are necessary for plants and are called essential elements as ( C , H , O , N , P , S , K ), ( Mg , Ca , Fe , Cu , B , Zn , Mn , Mo ) and ( Cl ). These essential elements are categorised into 2 groups as macro elements and micro elements. Marco elements are required by plants in larger amounts eg., ( C , H , O , N , S ), ( P , K , Ca , Mg ). Microelements or trace elements are required by plants in very small amounts ie in traces (e g )., ( Fe

125293.subject: Botany
125293.text: What are green plants called due to their ability to make their own food?
125293.sol: All animals including human beings depend on plants for their food. Have you ever wondered from where plants get their food? Green plants, in fact, have to make or rather synthesise the food they need and all other organisms depend on them for their needs. The green plants make or rather synthesise the food they need through photosynthesis and are therefore called autotrophs. You have already learnt that the autotrophic nutrition is found only in plants and all other organisms that depend on the green plants for fo

125396.text: To what does the primary acceptor of electrons transfer its electron?
125396.sol: As electrons move through the photosystems, protons are transported across the membrane. This happens because the primary accepter of electron which is located towards the outer side of the membrane transfers its electron not to an electron carrier but to an H carrier. Hence, this molecule removes a proton from the stroma while transporting an electron. When this molecule passes on its electron to the electron carrier on the inner side of the membrane, the proton is released into the inner side or the lumen side of

125416.text: Who discovered the first CO2 fixation product in the Calvin cycle?
125416.sol: CO2 is combined with H2O to produce (CH2O) n or sugars. It was of interest to scientists to find out how this reaction proceeded, or rather what was the first product formed when CO2 is taken into a reaction or fixed. Just after world war II, among the several efforts to put radioisotopes to beneficial use, the work of Melvin Calvin is exemplary . The use of radioactive 14C by him in algal photosynthesis studies led to the discovery that the first CO2 fixation product was a 3-carbon organic acid. He also contribute

125848.text: What is the elongated slender part beneath the stigma called?
125848.sol: The gynoecium represents the female reproductive part of the flower. The gynoecium may consist of a single pistil (monocarpellary) or may have more than one pistil (multicarpellary). When there are more than one, the pistils may be fused together (syncarpous) or may be free (apocarpous) Each pistil has three parts the stigma, style and ovary. The stigma serves as a landing platform for pollen grains. The style is the elongated slender part beneath the stigma. The basal bulged part of the pistil is the ovary. Inside

126259.subject: Botany
126259.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Pollen grains are well preserved as fossils. Reason (R): The inner wall of the pollen grain, called intine, is highly resistant to strong acids and enzymes. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

126259.sol: Assertion (A) is true: Pollen grains are well preserved as fossils because of the presence of a highly resistant organic material called sporopollenin in their outer layer. Reason (R) is false: The inner wall of the pollen grain is the intine, which is a thin and continuous layer made up of cellulose and pectin. It is not highly resistant. The extreme resistance to high temperatures, strong acids, and enzymes is provided entirely by the outer layer, the exine, which is composed of sporopollenin. Therefore, Assertio

126356.subject: Botany
126356.text: The one advantage of cleistogamy is

seed dispersal is more efficient and wide spread
seed set is not dependent on pollinators
each visit of a pollinator results in transfer of hundreds of pollen grains
126356.sol: Cleistogamous flowers do not open so, they self-pollinate and thus, do not depend on pollinators.

126674.sol: Energy storage in plants (A) is provided by starch (2). Energy storage in animals (B) is stored in glycogen (1). Structural component of cell walls (C) is cellulose (3). Structural component of exoskeletons (D) is chitin (4).

Some tissues especially the neural tissues have lipids with more complex structures. (i) Lecithin found in the plasma membrane is a phospholipid, not a glycolipid. 127767.subject: Botany
127767.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The pyramid of energy can be inverted in a marine ecosystem. Reason (R): When energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next, some energy is always lost as heat at each step. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
127767.sol: The pyramid of energy is always upright and can never be inverted in any ecosystem, including marine ecosystems. This is because according to the 10 percent law and the second law of thermodynamics, when energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next, some energy is always lost as heat at each step. Therefore, the energy at a lower trophic level is always greater than at a higher level. Thus, the Assertion is incorrect, but the Reason is a correct statement. Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

128872.text: What is the function of the inter-atrial septum in the human heart?
options: To separate the right and left ventricles
To separate the right and left atria
To initiate and maintain rhythmic contractile activity
To divide into right and left bundle
128872.sol: A thin, muscular wall called the interatrial septum separates the right and the left atria, whereas a thick-walled, the inter-ventricular septum, separates the left and the right ventricles. The atrium and the ventricle of the same side are also separated by a thick fibrous tissue called the atrio-ventricular septum.

128894.subject: Zoology

128894.sol: This sequential event in the heart which is cyclically repeated is called the cardiac cycle and it consists of systole and diastole of both the atria and ventricles . As mentioned earlier, the heart beats 72 times per minute, i.e., that many cardiac cycles are performed per minute. From this it could be deduced that the duration of a cardiac cycle is 0.8 seconds. During a cardiac cycle , each ventricle pumps out approximately 70 mL of blood which is called the stroke volume. The stroke volume multiplied by the hear

129362.subject: Zoology
129362.text: During the propagation of a nerve impulse, the action potential results from the movement of
options: Na ⁺ ions from extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid
Ka ⁺ ions from extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid
Na ⁺ ions from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid
Ka ⁺ ions from intracellular fluid to extracellular fluid
129362.sol: When the threshold stimulus is applied, the permeability of the membrane for sodium ions will change. Voltage gated sodium ion channels open and Na ⁺ ion flows form extracellular fluid to intracellular fluid, the outside becomes negative and inside positive. The membrane is depolarised & when the two ends of this membrane is connected to oscilloscope a potential difference of +30 mv , called as action potential is generated.

129967.subject: Zoology

131438.sol: In eukaryotes, this organization is much more complex. There is a set of positively charged, basic proteins called histones. A protein acquires charge depending upon the abundance of amino acids residues with charged side chains. Histones are rich in the basic amino acid residues lysine and arginine. Both the amino acid residues carry positive charges in their side chains. Histones are organized to form a unit of eight molecules called histone octamer. The negatively charged DNA is wrapped around the positively cha

131459.subject: Zoology
131459.text: What was the result of Hershey and Chase's experiments regarding the presence of radioactive DNA in the viruses?
options: Radioactive DNA was present in viruses grown on radioactive sulfur
Radioactive DNA was not present in any of the viruses
Radioactive DNA was present in viruses grown on radioactive phosphorus
Radioactive DNA was present in both types of viruses
131459.sol: The unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material came from the experiments of Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase (1952). They worked with viruses that infect bacteria called bacteriophages. The bacteriophage attaches to the bacteria and its genetic material then enters the bacterial cell. The bacterial cell treats the viral genetic material as if it was its own and subsequently manufactures more virus particles. Hershey and Chase worked to discover whether it was protein or DNA from the viruses that entered the

If Assertion is true but Reason is false

Thomas Hunt Morgan and Barbara McClintock
132182.sol: In 1900, three Scientists (de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak) independently rediscovered Mendel’s results on the inheritance of characters. Also, by this time due to advancements in microscopy that were taking place, scientists were able to carefully observe cell division. This led to the discovery of structures in the nucleus that appeared to double and divide just before each cell division. These were called chromosomes (colored bodies, as they were visualised by staining). By 1902, the chromosome movement duri

132380.subject: Zoology

132380.sol: Law of Dominance: One allele dominates over another in heterozygous condition. Law of Segregation: Alleles segregate during gamete formation. options: Structures that perform similar functions but are anatomically different
Structures that are anatomically similar and indicate common ancestry
Structures that evolved independently in different species
Structures that are present only in specific environments
132684.sol: Divergent evolution refers to similar anatomical structures in different species that evolve to perform different functions due to adaptations.Such similarities can be interpreted to understand whether common ancestors were shared or not. For example whales, bats, Cheetah and human (all mammals) share similarities in the pattern of bones of forelimbs. 132686.subject: Zoology
132686.text: What does analogy refer to in evolutionary terms?
options: Similar anatomical structures due to common ancestry
Different structures evolving for similar functions
Similar functions due to different evolutionary origins
Structures that have no evolutionary significance
132686.sol: Analogy refers to different structures that evolve to perform similar functions, resulting from convergent evolution. Wings of butterfly and of birds look alike. They are not anatomically similar structures though they perform similar functions. Hence, analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution - different structures evolving for the same function and hence having similarity. Other examples of analogy are the eye of the octopus and of mammals or the flippers of Penguins and Dolphins. One can say that

133126.subject: Zoology
133126.text: Which have not left any evidences of organic evolution?
133126.sol: The organisms which possess the characters of two different groups are called connecting links. They provide the evidence of organic evolution. Examples : (1) Archaeopteryx is connecting link between reptiles and birds. (2) Neopilina is connecting link between Annelida and Mollusca. (3) Peripatus is connecting link between Annelida and Arthropoda.

133173.subject: Zoology
133173.text: What is the role of the female Anopheles mosquito in the life cycle of Plasmodium?
133173.sol: Malaria is caused by a tiny protozoan named Plasmodium. Malignant malaria, which is the most serious form of malaria, is caused by Plasmodium falciparum. Plasmodium enters the human body as sporozoites (infectious form) through the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquito. The female Anopheles mosquito is the vector (transmitting agent) in the life cycle of Plasmodium . 133615.subject: Zoology
133615.sol: AIDS or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome or acquired immune deficiency syndrome (a death warrant) is a serious disease (also called slim disease) caused by a retrovirus HIV (human immunodeficiency virus). It is a set of symptoms and infections resulting from the damage to the human immune system by the virus, that depletes primarily the number of Tlymphocytes (CD-4 T cells or helper T-cells) and renders the patient susceptible to opportunistic infections i.e., infection caused by nonpathogens.

134434.sol: In the same way, a plasmid can be used as vector to deliver an alien piece of DNA into the host organism. The linking of antibiotic resistance gene with the plasmid vector became possible with the enzyme DNA ligase, which acts on cut DNA molecules and joins their ends. This makes a new combination of circular autonomously replicating DNA created in vitro and is known as recombinant DNA .

135106.sol: Populations evolve to maximize their reproductive fitness, also called Darwinian fitness (high r value), in the habitat in which they live. 6a13e46a688ac6d0667aad95.sol: Klinefelter's syndrome is a chromosomal disorder caused by the presence of an additional copy of the X-chromosome, resulting in a karyotype of 47 , XXY. 6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a25.subject: Biology
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a25.text: According to Erwin Chargaff's rules for a double-stranded DNA molecule, which of the following relationships is universally correct?
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a25.sol: According to Erwin Chargaff's rules for a double-stranded DNA molecule, the amount of adenine ( A ) is always equal to the amount of thymine ( T ), and the amount of guanine ( G ) is always equal to the amount of cytosine ( C ). A = T and G = C Adding these two equations, we get: A + G = T + C This means the total amount of purines ( A + G ) is equal to the total amount of pyrimidines ( C + T ). A + G C + T = 1 Answer: A + G C + T = 1

95409.sol: Examples of Class Aves: Flying birds - Passer (Sparrow), Corvus (Crow), Psittacula (Parrot), Columba (Pigeon), Pavo (Peacock National bird), Neophron (Vulture). Flightless birds (Ratitae group) - Struthio (Ostrich), Rhea, Emu. Others - Aptenodytes (Penguin).

95580.subject: Botany
95580.text: Which of the following organisms is radially symmetrical?
95580.sol: Radial Symmetry: A radial animal has a top and a bottom (or an oral and aboral side), but has no head end or rear end and no left or right.

95823.subject: Botany
95823.text: Which of the following changes in earlier classification systems were not brought about by R.H. Whittaker?
options: Blue green algae are no longer considered as plants.
Chlorella , a unicellular alga, is no longer considered as a plant.
Amoeba and Paramoecium are no longer considered as animals.
Yeast, a unicellular eukaryote, is no longer considered as fungus
95823.sol: R.H. Whittaker proposed a Five Kingdom Classification in 1969. According to him all unicellular prokaryotic organisms like Bacteria, BGA are included in Kingdom Monera and second kingdom Protista includes all unicellular eukaryotic organisms like Amoeba, Paramecium, etc., kingdom Fungi includes saprophytic, eukaryotic mostly multicellular organisms (except unicellular Saccharomyces cerevisiae ). All multicellular organisms whose cell wall is made up of cellulose and pectin and are mostly autotrophic are included in

96137.subject: Botany
96137.text: The eubacterial cellular part that is similar to a eukaryotic cell is ____
96137.sol: Eubacteria are prokaryotic but are enclosed by plasma membrane like the eukaryotic cells. The composition and architecture of the plasma membrane remain the same for all cells. Ribosomes are of 70S type in bacteria. The cell wall has peptidoglycan as the main component. The prokaryotes are devoid of the true nucleus.

96389.subject: Botany
options: Pyramid of energy for grassland and pyramid of biomass for a lake
Pyramid of biomass for grassland and pyramid of number for tree
Pyramid of number for sea and pyramid of biomass for grassland
Pyramid of energy and biomass for a pond
96389.sol: In the grassland ecosystem, the pyramid of numbers is upright or straight. The producers are mainly grasses are always more in number. The primary consumers as grasshoppers, rabbits, mice etc. Are Lesser than the number of grasses. The primary consumers are eaten by a relatively smaller number of secondary consumers as a frog, lizard, snake etc. These secondary consumers are consumed by only a few tertiary or top consumers as the hawk, peacock or other birds.

96459.subject: Botany
96459.text: Identify the likely organisms (1), (2), (3) and (4) in the food web shown below.
96459.sol: Food web is a network of food chains or feeding relationships by which energy, and nutrients are passed on from one species of living organisms to another.

96567.subject: Botany
96567.text: Rate of biomass production is expressed as:
options: k c a l m - 2 y r - 1
k c a l g m 2 y r - 1
96567.sol: The amount of biomass produced per unit area over a period of time is called primary productivity expressed in weight ( g – 2 ) or energy k c a l m – 2 . The rate at which this biomass is produced is called productivity. To compare the productivity of different ecosystems it is expressed by units g – 2 y r – 1 or k c a l m – 2 y r – 1 . It is divided into gross primary productivity and net primary productivity. The rate at which organic matter is produced during photosynthesis is gross primary productivity and the

96663.subject: Botany
96663.text: Which one is NOT correctly matched?
options: Net primary productivity - available biomass for consumption
Secondary productivity - formation of new organic matter in producer
96663.sol: Gross primary production (GPP) is the rate at which an ecosystem's producers capture and store a given amount of chemical energy as biomass in a given length of time. (Definition). It is also the rate of conversion of light energy to chemical energy by producers in an ecosystem. The rate of assimilation of food energy by consumers is called secondary productivity and this energy is available to carnivores as they are the consumers.

97021.subject: Botany
97021.text: Match the following and choose the correct combination from the options given. Column I Column II A . Mustard 1 . Polyadelphy B . Brinjal 2 . Diadelphy C . Citrus 3 . Variations in the length of filaments D . Pea 4 . Epipetalous stamens
97021.sol: Pisum sativum , beans, gram etc. belong to family Fabaceae and root of all members of Fabaceae contains root nodules that have nitrogen fixing bacteria and they shows the presence of diadelphous stamen whereas potato, tomato, brinjal are included in family Solanaceae which shows bicarpellary, syncarpous and superior ovary and their Stamens are five in number, epipetalous (stamens attached to petals)

97075.subject: Botany
97075.text: Match the column and select the correct option. Column-I Column-II (1) Leaf tendril (i) Cactus (2) Leaf Spine (ii) Pea (3) Stem tendril (iii) Bougainvillea (4) Stem thorn (iv) Gourds (v) Turmeric
97075.sol: Stem tendrils which develop from axillary buds, are slender and spirally coiled and help plants to climb such as in gourds (cucumber, pumpkins, watermelon) and grapevines. Axillary buds of stems may also get modified into woody, straight and pointed thorns. Thorns are found in many plants such as Citrus and Bougainvillea. Leaves are often modified to perform functions other than photosynthesis. They are converted into tendrils for climbing as in peas or into spines for defence as in cacti

97503.subject: Botany
97503.sol: Ulothrix and Spirogyra belong to the class Chlorophyceae, commonly called green algae. Ulothrix , found in freshwater and marine water, is generally found attached to the bed of water bodies. The cells are very long and broad and favour low temperature for growth. They attach themselves to the bed by a modified holdfast cell. Spirogyra on the other hand a free-living and form mass floating on surface of water bodies. They are generally found in freshwater region and named so due to their spiral form of chloroplast.

97543.subject: Botany
97543.text: Which of the following is the unique feature of bryophytes?
options: Reproduction only by the formation of gametes
97543.sol: They are the simplest and most primitive land plants and they require water to complete their life cycle. They are also known by the name of amphibians of the plant kingdom and are found in moist and shady places. They possess rhizoids to absorb water from the soil. The gametophytic generation in bryophytes is long-lived while sporophytic generation is short-lived so the sporophyte is completely dependent on the gametophyte for nutrition. Vascular tissue is completely absent in Bryophytes.

97601.subject: Botany
97601.text: In anaerobic glycolysis, 2 molecules of inorganic phosphate are used per molecule of glucose consumed. Which of the following enzyme catalyzes the uptake of inorganic phosphate?
97601.sol: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (GAPDH) is a very important enzyme in the production of energy. This enzyme catalyzes the sixth step in the process of breaking down glucose, also known as glycolysis which occurs in organisms of all phyla. The sixth step consists of the oxidation of Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate by NAD and inorganic phosphate to yield 1,3 bisphosphoglycerate

97647.subject: Botany
97647.text: The crucial requirement for the process of chemiosmosis is
97647.sol: Chemiosmosis requires a membrane, a proton pump, a proton gradient and ATPase. Energy is used to pump protons across the membrane to create a gradient or a high concentration of protons within the thylakoid lumen. However, the most essential requirement is the creation of a proton gradient across the membrane.

97859.subject: Botany
97859.text: The framework system of classification in which various taxonomic categories are arranged in order of logical sequence is called
97859.sol: Systematics (L-system: order). The comparative study of organisms based on morphology, anatomy, ecology, physiology, biochemistry, etc. is known as systematics. This comprises three fields such as 1. Nomenclature 2. Classification and 3. Taxonomy Systematics is also the science of diversity of organisms from an evolutionary context.

97965.subject: Botany
97965.text: In flowering plants, the substances that would need to be transported are:
97965.sol: In a flowering plant, the substances that would need to be transported are water, mineral nutrients, organic nutrients and plant growth regulators.

98420.subject: Chemistry
98420.text: On analysis of a protein chain, it was found that it is made up of just a peptide bond. The possible structure of the protein is its
98420.sol: Proteins contain amino acids joined by peptide bonds. This protein structure can be primary, secondary, tertiary or quaternary. The primary structure is the simplest structure in which position of amino acids can be checked. Thus these structures contain only peptide bonds. The secondary structure is coiling of primary structure i.e. polypeptide chain. These can be alpha helix or beta pleated sheets that show presence of hydrogen bonding apart from the peptide bond. Tertiary structures are woollen ball appearance o

98445.subject: Chemistry
98445.text: After which of the following treatments (I-III) would an enzyme still be expected to have activity? I. Protease treatment. II. Heating almost to the point of denaturation. III. Freezing and then thawing once only.
98445.sol: Protease enzymes have catalytic function. When this is added to other enzymes it will catalyse the peptide bonds of the enzymes and thus will result in denaturation of the enzymes. Similarly heating the enzymes will also increase the temperature and this will result in denaturation too because enzymes are active only at optimum temperatures and beyond it there will not be any function. However freezing has no effect on enzyme activity as it does not affect the peptide bonds.
